text:
Noah Cates got his headline moment on Nov. 21, breaking a tie in Montreal with 31 seconds left for the Flyers' third straight win. That's not usually how his value shows up. He plays 13:33 a night in a checking role, and Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.1 wins above replacement last season, 47th among 401 forwards, most of it on the penalty kill. Opponents got 0.19 fewer expected goals per 60 with him on the ice, a 97th-percentile number.

This season the defensive side still holds. Philadelphia's share of 5-on-5 chance quality is almost 9 points better with him on than off. The points are the soft spot: 9 in 27 games after 47 last season. Some of that is bad luck. The Flyers have scored 5.9 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and that kind of gap usually closes. Our numbers project about 36 points, with the late winner a reminder that he'll get a few big ones along the way.
headline: Noah Cates, the Flyers' quiet chance-killer, finds a late winner
